stem: What does it mean for software to be "secure by default"?

options.A: It ships with every feature enabled so that users can choose what to turn off later
options.B: It ships with secure settings enabled, so users must opt in to riskier options
options.C: It passes an independent security certification first
options.D: It includes a hardening guide explaining safe settings

explanation: Secure-by-default products protect users out of the box, for example with MFA on, unused services off, and no default passwords.

distractor_rationales.C: Certification can happen either way. Secure by default is about the settings it ships with.
distractor_rationales.D: A guide still relies on users to secure it. Secure by default means it ships that way.

stem: Which development model pairs each development phase with a matching testing phase, such as requirements with acceptance testing?

options.A: Spiral model built around repeated risk-driven loops
options.B: Agile Scrum with two-week sprints and a product backlog
options.C: V-model
options.D: Code-and-fix with no formal phases

explanation: The V-model extends waterfall by linking each specification phase on one side of the V to a verification phase on the other.

distractor_rationales.A: Spiral is organized around risk-driven iterations.
distractor_rationales.B: Scrum uses iterative sprints rather than paired phases.

stem: What is the main purpose of cryptographically signing commits in a source code repository?

options.A: To link each commit to the specific change ticket that approved it
options.B: To make the commit history impossible to rewrite
options.C: To prove the code was reviewed before merging
options.D: To verify who authored each commit and that it is unaltered

explanation: Commit signatures let reviewers and tools confirm that a change came from a trusted developer key, which helps detect impersonated or tampered commits.

distractor_rationales.A: Ticket links are commit message conventions, not cryptographic proof.
distractor_rationales.B: History can still be rewritten. Signatures let others detect unsigned or altered commits.
distractor_rationales.C: A signature proves authorship, not that anyone reviewed the code.

stem: Who should be allowed to change the CI/CD pipeline definitions that build and deploy production software?

options.A: Only authorized people, with changes reviewed like code
options.B: Any developer, with changes logged for a later audit
options.C: Only the security team, who edit pipelines on request
options.D: Any developer who has write access to the code repository

explanation: Pipeline definitions control what reaches production. Changes should be restricted and reviewed so no one can quietly add malicious steps or skip checks.

distractor_rationales.B: Logging after the fact does not stop a malicious pipeline change from deploying.
distractor_rationales.C: Centralizing every edit in security creates a bottleneck. Authorized owners with review work better.
distractor_rationales.D: Write access without review lets one person change how production software is built.

stem: Which are common standard formats for a software bill of materials?

options.A: JSON Web Token and SAML
options.B: SPDX and CycloneDX
options.C: CVSS and EPSS
options.D: STIX and TAXII

explanation: SPDX and CycloneDX are widely used, machine-readable SBOM formats that list components, versions, and relationships.

distractor_rationales.A: JWT and SAML are identity token formats.
distractor_rationales.D: STIX and TAXII describe and exchange threat intelligence.

stem: A code review finds that the login handler logs the full request body, including users' passwords, for debugging. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Encrypt the log file with the same key used for the database
options.B: Keep the logging but delete log files every month
options.C: Remove or redact sensitive fields before anything is logged
options.D: Move the logs to a folder that only developers can open

explanation: Secrets should never be written to logs. Redacting sensitive fields at the source prevents exposure to anyone who reads or collects logs.

distractor_rationales.A: Encryption still leaves passwords in readable form to anyone with the key.
distractor_rationales.B: Monthly deletion leaves weeks of exposure.
distractor_rationales.D: Developers should not see users' passwords either.

stem: Which component commonly provides central authentication, rate limiting, and routing for many backend APIs?

options.A: A content delivery network cache
options.B: A database connection pool
options.C: A message queue broker
options.D: An API gateway

explanation: An API gateway sits in front of backend services and applies shared controls such as authentication, rate limiting, and logging.

distractor_rationales.A: A CDN caches content, mainly for performance.
distractor_rationales.B: A connection pool manages database connections.
distractor_rationales.C: A message broker passes messages between services.

stem: Which release technique runs two identical production environments and switches traffic from the old one to the new one, allowing a quick switch back?

options.A: Blue-green deployment
options.B: Canary release to a small share of users
options.C: Rolling update across servers one at a time
options.D: Feature flags that switch code paths on and off

explanation: Blue-green deployment keeps the previous version ready, so a failed release can be rolled back simply by switching traffic back.

distractor_rationales.B: A canary sends some traffic to a new version, not a switch between two whole environments.
distractor_rationales.C: A rolling update replaces servers gradually and has no idle second environment to switch back to.
distractor_rationales.D: Feature flags control features in code, not whole environments.

stem: A quick prototype built to demonstrate an idea was so popular that the business wants to put it straight into production. What should happen?

options.A: Deploy it as is, since users are already happy with it
options.B: Treat it as a prototype and apply full security design and testing
options.C: Deploy it but hide it from search engines until it is reviewed
options.D: Rewrite only its user interface and deploy the rest of it unchanged

explanation: Prototypes usually skip security work. Before production, the design and code need the same reviews and testing as any other system.

distractor_rationales.A: Happy users do not mean the code is secure.
distractor_rationales.C: Hiding it does not fix security weaknesses.
distractor_rationales.D: Security flaws are often in the back end, not the interface.

stem: Which set of business functions does OWASP SAMM use to organize software assurance practices?

options.A: Identify, protect, detect, respond, and recover
options.B: Plan, do, check, and act
options.C: Governance, design, implementation, verification, and operations
options.D: Initial, repeatable, defined, managed, and optimizing

explanation: SAMM groups its security practices under five business functions that follow the software lifecycle and its governance.

distractor_rationales.A: These are the original five NIST Cybersecurity Framework functions (CSF 2.0 adds Govern), not SAMM's business functions.
distractor_rationales.B: This is the Deming improvement cycle.
distractor_rationales.D: These are Capability Maturity Model levels.

stem: A developer's personal access token with full rights to every repository in the organization was leaked in a public forum post. What should be done now and for the future?

options.A: Revoke the token and issue an identical full-access token
options.B: Keep the token active but alert on every use of it
options.C: Remove the developer's access to all repositories permanently
options.D: Revoke the token, and require narrowly scoped, short-lived tokens

explanation: A leaked token must be revoked at once. Fine-grained tokens that expire limit the damage of any future leak.

distractor_rationales.A: Revocation stops this leak, but another full-access token repeats the risk. Tokens should be narrow and short-lived.
distractor_rationales.B: The leaked token is usable by anyone, so it must be revoked, not just watched.
distractor_rationales.C: Permanent removal is disproportionate; the token was the problem.

stem: A pipeline uses several third-party build actions referenced by the tag "latest." What is the BEST improvement?

options.A: Pin each action to a reviewed commit hash
options.B: Pin each action to a version tag such as v2 or v3
options.C: Fork the actions and keep using their latest tag in the fork
options.D: Scan the actions' repositories for known vulnerabilities

explanation: A floating tag can change underneath the pipeline. Pinning to an immutable reference means only reviewed code runs with access to pipeline secrets.

distractor_rationales.B: Tags can be moved to point at new code. A commit hash cannot.
distractor_rationales.C: A fork pinned to "latest" still pulls whatever lands there next.
distractor_rationales.D: Scanning finds known issues but does not stop a tag being repointed to malicious code.

stem: Which technology runs inside an application at runtime and can detect and block attacks, such as injection, as they happen?

options.A: Static application security testing of source code
options.B: Runtime application self-protection (RASP)
options.C: Software composition analysis
options.D: Manual threat modeling

explanation: RASP instruments the running application so it can see how input is used and block attacks in context.

distractor_rationales.A: SAST analyzes code before it runs.
distractor_rationales.D: Threat modeling is a design activity.

stem: A vendor now delivers an SBOM with each release of its product. What is the BEST way to use it?

options.A: Review it once, when the product is first purchased and deployed
options.B: Keep it with the contract for auditors to request
options.C: Ingest it and check its components continuously for new flaws
options.D: Compare it only with the previous release's SBOM

explanation: An SBOM is valuable when it is monitored. Matching components against new vulnerability data shows quickly when the product is affected.

distractor_rationales.A: New vulnerabilities appear after purchase. The SBOM needs continuous checking.
distractor_rationales.B: Filing it away gives no early warning of new flaws.
distractor_rationales.D: Comparing releases shows changes but does not check components against new advisories.

stem: A SaaS scheduling tool asks for administrator-level OAuth access to the company's whole email tenant, although it only needs to read calendars. What should the company do?

options.A: Grant it, but monitor the app's mailbox access in the logs
options.B: Grant it for a 90-day trial with a review afterward
options.C: Grant it once the vendor signs a data processing agreement
options.D: Require narrower permissions, or reject the tool if it cannot comply

explanation: Third-party apps should get only the access their function needs. Tenant-wide admin rights would expose all mail if the vendor were compromised.

distractor_rationales.A: Monitoring does not reduce the excessive access.
distractor_rationales.B: Even a trial gives tenant-wide email access the tool does not need.
distractor_rationales.C: A contract helps, but least privilege still requires narrower permissions.

stem: A web application's JavaScript bundle contains an API secret for a paid third-party service. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Move the call to the backend so the secret stays on the server
options.B: Obfuscate the JavaScript bundle so the secret is harder for users to spot
options.C: Restrict the secret to the app's domain using CORS
options.D: Rotate the secret every week and keep it in the bundle

explanation: Anything sent to the browser can be read. Calls that need secrets belong on the server, which holds the secret and exposes only a safe interface.

distractor_rationales.B: Obfuscation delays but does not prevent extraction.
distractor_rationales.C: CORS controls browsers, not someone copying the secret and calling the service directly.
distractor_rationales.D: Each new secret is exposed in the bundle just the same.

stem: An order form multiplies quantity by price using a fixed-size integer. A tester enters a huge quantity, and the total wraps around to a negative number, creating a credit. What is the weakness and fix?

options.A: Cross-site scripting; encode the output shown on the order page
options.B: Integer overflow; validate input ranges and use checked arithmetic
options.C: SQL injection; use parameterized queries when saving the order total
options.D: Race condition; lock the order record during checkout

explanation: Values that exceed the integer's range wrap around. Enforcing sensible input limits and overflow-checked arithmetic prevents the error.

distractor_rationales.D: Nothing here involves timing. A huge number wrapped around the integer's range.

stem: After login, an application redirects users to whatever URL is in the "next" parameter. Attackers send links that redirect to a phishing site. What is the BEST fix?

options.A: Show users a warning page before any external redirect
options.B: Encrypt the "next" parameter with a shared key in the URL
options.C: Allow redirects only to an allow-list of internal paths
options.D: Strip the http:// prefix from the next parameter

explanation: Open redirects lend the trusted domain's credibility to attacker sites. Restricting redirect targets to known internal destinations removes the abuse.

distractor_rationales.A: A warning still forwards users to the attacker's site, and many click through.
distractor_rationales.B: Encryption does not validate the destination.
distractor_rationales.D: Attackers can use //evil.com or other forms. Only allow-listed internal paths are safe.

stem: A public GraphQL API allows deeply nested queries, and a single crafted query recently exhausted server resources. What is the BEST control?

options.A: Rate-limit each client to 100 requests per minute
options.B: Cache the results of any repeated GraphQL queries at the server
options.C: Require authentication for all API clients
options.D: Enforce query depth and cost limits; restrict introspection

explanation: Limiting depth and cost stops resource-exhaustion queries, and restricting introspection reduces what attackers can learn about the schema.

distractor_rationales.A: Rate limiting still limits how many expensive queries arrive, but one crafted query can exhaust resources, so request counts alone are insufficient.
distractor_rationales.B: Attackers send new queries that are not cached.
distractor_rationales.C: Authentication helps attribution, but any authenticated client can still send the crafted query.

stem: A penetration test two weeks before launch finds an architectural flaw that requires redesign. What is the BEST response now and for future projects?

options.A: Have the owner make a documented risk decision; review designs earlier
options.B: Launch on schedule and plan the redesign for a later release
options.C: Delay launch until the redesign is done, whatever the cost
options.D: Add compensating controls and launch without telling the owner

explanation: The risk owner must decide whether to delay, mitigate, or accept with full information. Earlier threat modeling and design review keep such flaws from surfacing so late.

distractor_rationales.B: Launching without a documented risk decision leaves no one accountable for the flaw.
distractor_rationales.C: Delay may be right, but that is the business owner's decision once the risk is weighed.
distractor_rationales.D: Hiding the risk from the owner removes their decision.

stem: Leadership plans to use software security maturity scores to rank teams and cut bonuses for the lowest scorers. What is the BEST advice?

options.A: Proceed, since pressure is the fastest way to raise scores
options.B: Use scores to guide improvement and investment, not to punish teams
options.C: Keep the scores secret from teams so they cannot game them
options.D: Stop measuring maturity altogether, since teams dislike being assessed

explanation: Punitive use encourages inflated self-assessments and hides problems. Maturity scores are most useful for finding gaps and directing support.

distractor_rationales.A: Pressure tends to produce gaming, not real improvement.
distractor_rationales.C: Secret scores cannot guide team improvement.

stem: Developers can push container images directly to the production registry, bypassing the pipeline's tests and scans. What is the BEST control?

options.A: Ask developers to run the tests locally before pushing images
options.B: Scan the production registry once a month for any vulnerable images
options.C: Deploy only pipeline-signed images, enforced by admission control
options.D: Require two developers to approve each direct push

explanation: Signing images in the pipeline and verifying signatures at deployment means only artifacts that passed the pipeline can run in production.

distractor_rationales.B: Monthly scans detect problems long after deployment.
distractor_rationales.D: Two approvers still bypass the pipeline's tests and scans.

stem: A DAST scan of a single-page application reports few findings, but most of the app's functions are backend API calls the crawler never discovered. What is the BEST improvement?

options.A: Run the same scan more often with the default settings
options.B: Replace DAST with a review of the front-end HTML files
options.C: Add a WAF in front of the API instead of scanning it
options.D: Give the scanner the API specification and authenticated sessions

explanation: Crawlers struggle with script-heavy apps. Supplying an OpenAPI definition and valid sessions lets the scanner test the real API surface.

distractor_rationales.A: Repeating a scan with the same coverage gap finds nothing new.
distractor_rationales.B: The front-end HTML does not include backend API logic.
distractor_rationales.C: A WAF is a protective layer, not a test of the undiscovered API functions.

stem: A vendor's software update added telemetry that sends customer names to the vendor's servers, which the contract does not allow. What is the BEST response and prevention?

options.A: Block the telemetry, enforce the contract, and stage future updates
options.B: Accept it, since vendors decide what their products collect
options.C: Stop applying any future updates from the vendor at all
options.D: Uninstall the product immediately without any assessment

explanation: The company must stop the unauthorized flow and hold the vendor to its terms. Testing updates in staging, including their network behavior, catches such changes earlier.

distractor_rationales.B: The contract governs what data the vendor may collect.
distractor_rationales.C: Skipping updates leaves security flaws unpatched.
distractor_rationales.D: Removal may be needed later, but first stop the flow and assess.

stem: A security hotfix was applied on a release branch, but the next regular release reintroduced the vulnerability because the fix never reached the main branch. What is the BEST process fix?

options.A: Document every hotfix carefully in the release notes
options.B: Merge every hotfix into the main branch and add a regression test
options.C: Re-run the penetration test before each release
options.D: Keep a list of hotfixes and check it before each release

explanation: Hotfixes must flow back to the main line, and a regression test confirms the vulnerability does not return in later releases.

distractor_rationales.A: Documentation does not put the fix into the main branch.
distractor_rationales.C: Testing may catch the regression, but late. Merging and a regression test prevent it.
distractor_rationales.D: A manual list depends on people. Merging with a regression test makes it automatic.
